name: THE LETTER-WRITER
note: Doc 07 #1. Writes letters home for men who can't. Charges by the page. Resolves the notice board hotspot. Doing better than anyone, because he sells the one thing that never runs out.

barks.R_NOBODY: Letters home. Ten cents the page.
barks.R_SWINDLED: Letters home. Might want to leave a bit out.
barks.R_RACCOON: I could make the raccoon sound better.
barks.R_SURVEYED: ‘Had my land surveyed by a professional.’ See? Free of charge.
barks.R_BORDERS_MOTT: Now you’ve got something to write about. Twenty cents.
barks.R_LOST_DUEL: I’d leave the duel out entirely.
barks.R_WON_DUEL: Beat Deke Vessel. That’s a page and a half right there.
barks.R_DEAD: Do you want me to write to her, or would that be strange?
barks.R_TRUTH: Twelve years I’ve been making things up on this street and you did it in one afternoon.

sprite.note: Frames 0-1 are the idle: the pose and a derived one-pixel breath. Frames 2-4 are the three poses from the character sheet. `breaks` are SEPARATE actions chosen from a pool, each leaving the idle and returning to it -- not a routine played in order, which is what the eye catches.

migrationNote: ERRATA 54, x6. Was (30, 112) in the 320x144 play area. THE AMBIENT LAYER WAS NEVER MIGRATED: tools/migrate-play-area-x6.mjs is an ALLOWLIST -- "anything not on the list is left exactly as it was" -- and it measured "17 rooms, 140 rects". An ambient character is not a room, so nothing named these and nothing touched them. Every one of them stood in the sky, 13-15% down a 864-tall play area, for as long as errata 54 has been in force, and the game loaded and validated and drew them there.
placeNote: Back at the west end, beside the posted notices rather than clustered at the saloon with the other two. Was (2500, 712). THE CLUSTER WAS A MISTAKE OF MY OWN MAKING: I moved all three east on the reasoning that the saloon is the only lit thing at night, and the measurement says otherwise -- the mud at the Company and the Clarion reads 70-72 against the map seller’s 58, and only the saloon porch peaks at 84. Half a 3700px street had nobody in it. He belongs here anyway: doc 05 gives POSTED NOTICES to him, and a man who writes letters for the illiterate sets up where the town reads. Clear of the board rect and the Company steps.

props.note: HIS WORK STATION, drawn in the same operation and cut apart from him afterwards: the folding table with weighted paper, ink and spare pens, and the satchel of finished letters on the ground at its foot. A prop of the room at its own coordinates, standing to his right with its feet on his own floor row.

sprite.note: PHASE 2A: one frame, and that is the phase, not an omission. Static staging first, and Tyler accepts the face in the room before any life is animated on it -- doc 36 Q128. The sheet is pre-scaled to the height this room asks for where the character stands, so the engine draws it at about 1:1 instead of shrinking a 1200 px painting on every frame.

main_street_candidate.note: Beside the posted notices at the west end, where doc 07 and his own placeNote put him. SEATED AT HIS WORK now, not standing beside it: on his camp stool, leaning over the board on his knee, pen down on the paper mid-word, the far hand holding the sheet. `stature` 0.72 is a seated man with his boots flat -- anatomy, not taste. The station stands to his right at 1548,658 with the ink, the spare pens and the satchel.
